title: The Liturgical Year — a Catholic calendar wheel
description: An SVG wheel of the Roman Catholic liturgical year, from the First Sunday of Advent round to the eve of the next, with every day in its liturgical colour and Easter found by the Gregorian computus. You can pick any year from 1970 to 2299, see a today marker, tap a day for its proper name (for example 'Wednesday of the 25th Week in Ordinary Time'), open season details and browse 30+ movable and fixed feasts with their transfer rules applied.
prompt: My faith is a big part of my life and I've built Catholic recipe and directory sites, so I want a beautiful, correct circular calendar of the liturgical year. Draw it as an SVG wheel for any year, defaulting to the current one: Advent violet, Christmas white, Ordinary Time green, Lent violet, the Triduum, Easter white, Pentecost red. Compute Easter with the Gregorian computus and derive Ash Wednesday, Pentecost, the First Sunday of Advent, Christ the King and the rest, following US norms where they differ. Add a year picker, a today marker, and clicking a segment or day should show details. It must be right, so verify Easter against known dates in the tests.

methodology: Oracle testing against published data: Easter for ten years (1981 to 2285) plus the full set of 2026 movable feasts are hard-coded from real calendars, never from the page's own functions.

Rule-edge tests for the transfer logic, each tied to a real year: Annunciation 2024 (Holy Week), St Joseph 2023 (Sunday of Lent) and 2008 (Holy Week), Baptism of the Lord 2023 (Epiphany on 8 January), Immaculate Conception 2024 (Sunday), John the Baptist 2022 (Sacred Heart clash).
Time-dependent behaviour (today marker, default year, rollover at Advent) driven with page.clock.install plus pauseAt on three fixed dates.
Interaction tests for season segments by mouse, touch and keyboard (Enter on a focused SVG group), plus day stepping with arrow keys across the Easter to Ordinary Time boundary.
Input boundary checks: the year is clamped to 1970–2299 from typing and from the stepper.
Visual review at 1280px and 390px for label placement on the ring, especially bottom-half labels that are flipped to read left to right.
risks: Off-by-one errors at season boundaries (Holy Thursday, the Monday after Pentecost, the Saturday before Advent).
Timezone drift turning a local midnight into the previous UTC day; all maths uses integer UTC day numbers to avoid it.
Week numbering in the second part of Ordinary Time, which is counted backwards from Christ the King (week 34).
Rare collisions between fixed solemnities and movable feasts beyond the rules implemented.
qa.playwright: This page is pure calendar maths, so the most valuable tests are oracle comparisons with dates from real published calendars, read from data-iso attributes on the feast table instead of parsing formatted text. Time was the hard part: 'today' decides the default year and marker, so each scenario installs a fake clock and immediately pauses it with pauseAt before navigating, which keeps the date fixed without replaying frames. The SVG wheel was straightforward because segments are real focusable elements with data-testid attributes, so clicks and Enter presses need no coordinates. toHaveScreenshot was not used because layout and font rendering differ between desktop and the Pixel 7 profile; the wheel was reviewed by eye.
coverage: Computus against ten known Easter dates
All major 2026 movable feasts, the liturgical year span and the Sunday/weekday cycle
Today marker, day name and colour on three fake dates, including the Advent rollover
Season details by click, button and keyboard
Six transfer-rule edge cases from real years
Arrow-key day stepping and year clamping

a11y: Each season on the wheel is a focusable SVG group with role=button and a descriptive label, and it is duplicated as a real toggle button in the panel. The day card and season details are aria-live, the wheel itself accepts arrow keys to step through days, and every colour is also named in text.
